commodity_commentary: Commodity markets posted a mixed week with energy reversing while precious and base metals advanced — WTI fell 11.74% on the week to US$80.58/bbl and Brent fell 11.69% to US$83.23/bbl, reflecting the partial unwind of recent supply-shock premium that had carried crude above US$100/bbl a month earlier.37 Precious metals held firm as gold settled at US$4,353.30/oz (+26.87% year-over-year, monthly average down 4.44%) and silver at US$70.21/oz (+93.53% year-over-year, the steepest 52-week percentage advance of any commodity tracked here).37 Base metals firmed with copper at US$6.5085/lb (+35.59% year-over-year, within 2 cents of its 52-week high of US$6.6495/lb), driven by sustained Chinese industrial demand following the May NBS Manufacturing PMI reading of 50.0.25 Agricultural staples held with wheat at 586.25 cents per bushel (+0.51% on the week, +7.82% year-over-year) and the StatCan canola farm price at CAD$733.20 per tonne for the May reference.16 Lumber rose 2.55% on the week to US$623.50 per thousand board feet, the largest weekly percentage advance among forest products tracked here.37 The Signal Dispatch cross-reference engine ties commodity moves to 635 active Canadian mining projects ($184.5B aggregate), 89 oil and gas projects ($63.5B), and 269 forestry projects ($4.7B).37

commodities.name: Crude Oil (WTI)
commodities.context: WTI crude settled at US$80.58 per barrel on June 15, down 11.74% on the week and 23.56% on the month — the decline came as the geopolitical premium that had carried crude above US$100 per barrel a month earlier eased, following the Iran-war oil-price spike to four-year highs that the ECB cited as the operative motivation for its June 11 hike.26 The 52-week range runs US$55.27 to US$112.95 per barrel; WTI's +10.41% year-over-year reading sits above the 1-year average of US$72.33 per barrel.37 The Signal Dispatch cross-reference engine ties WTI to 89 active Canadian oil and gas projects ($63.5B aggregate). If WTI holds above US$74-76 per barrel, the typical Alberta oil-sands breakeven cluster cited in 2025 securities filings, the 89 oil and gas projects would maintain netbacks above that threshold.37

commodities.name: Crude Oil (Brent)
commodities.context: Brent crude settled at US$83.23 per barrel on June 15, down 11.69% on the week and 22.98% on the month — the move tracked WTI lower as the same supply-premium unwind played through the global benchmark, against a 52-week high of US$118.35 per barrel and a 1-year average at US$76.58 per barrel.37

commodities.name: Natural Gas
commodities.context: Natural gas settled at US$3.08 per million British thermal units on June 15, down 1.57% on the week and up 3.89% on the month — the year-over-year reading of -14.11% reflecting the easing of 2025 winter pricing, with the 52-week range running US$2.52 to US$7.46 per MMBtu and the 1-year average at US$3.40 per MMBtu.37 The Signal Dispatch cross-reference engine ties natural gas to 936 active power and energy projects ($614.3B aggregate), including LNG export terminals priced against a Henry Hub differential.37

commodities.name: Gold
commodities.context: Gold settled at US$4,353.30 per ounce on June 15, +0.05% on the week and +26.87% year-over-year — the 1-year advance ranks among the largest annual gains since the post-2020 reflation window, with the 52-week range running US$3,273.70 to US$5,318.40 per ounce.37 The Signal Dispatch cross-reference engine ties gold to 635 active Canadian mining projects ($184.5B aggregate), including Ontario, Quebec, and British Columbia gold producers whose all-in sustaining costs are cited in 2025 securities filings.37

commodities.name: Silver
commodities.context: Silver settled at US$70.21 per ounce on June 15, +2.77% on the week and +93.53% year-over-year — the year-over-year reading is the steepest 52-week percentage advance of any tracked commodity, against a 52-week high of US$115.08 per ounce and a 52-week low of US$35.70 per ounce.37

commodities.name: Copper
commodities.context: Copper settled at US$6.5085 per pound on June 15, +2.12% on the week and +35.59% year-over-year — the advance came as the May NBS Manufacturing PMI reading of 50.0 and the equipment manufacturing sub-index at 52.1 reflected sustained Chinese industrial demand, with the 52-week range running US$4.3300 to US$6.6495 per pound.25 The current print sits within 2 cents of the 52-week high.37

commodities.context: Pipeline data does not carry a current U3O8 spot reading — the timeseries.json uranium key holds a single stale point from May 19. Sector signals proxy via Cameco at CAD$100.96 on June 12 and the Sprott Physical Uranium Trust U-UN.TO unit at CAD$27.07, both equity proxies rather than spot U3O8.37

commodities.name: Nickel
commodities.context: Nickel registered a FRED monthly-average reading of US$18,879.23 per tonne, up 10.56% on the month — the monthly series is the only nickel signal available in pipeline data, as no spot-tracking series is currently active.37 The Signal Dispatch cross-reference engine ties nickel to the Ontario and Quebec battery materials supply chain, with 635 mining projects in the database carrying base-metal exposure.37
commodities.note: FRED monthly-average series (n=5 points). Label as monthly average, never spot.

commodities.name: Wheat
commodities.context: Wheat settled at 586.25 cents per bushel on June 15, +0.51% on the week, -8.00% on the month, and +7.82% year-over-year — the 52-week high of 668.25 cents per bushel and 52-week low of 495.00 cents per bushel bracket a 1-year average of 549.95 cents per bushel.37

commodities.name: Canola
commodities.context: Canola registered a StatCan farm-price reading of CAD$733.20 per tonne for the May 2026 reference — this is the StatCan 32-10-0077 monthly farm-price series, not a futures or spot quote, and feeds Prairie agricultural producer revenue calculations.16
commodities.note: StatCan 32-10-0077 farm price — monthly. Label farm price (monthly), never futures or spot.

commodities.name: Potash (Nutrien)
commodities.context: The Nutrien share-price proxy closed at CAD$94.61 on June 12, +1.05% on the week and +14.97% year-over-year — this is the NTR.TO equity price used as the potash sector proxy, not a US$-denominated potash spot price, with the 52-week range running CAD$75.58 to CAD$114.41.37
commodities.note: Nutrien (NTR.TO) share price proxy, CAD$ — NOT a US$ potash spot price.

commodities.name: Lumber
commodities.context: Lumber settled at US$623.50 per thousand board feet on June 12, +2.55% on the week and +8.06% on the month — the year-over-year reading of +0.73% sits roughly in line with the 1-year average of US$585.57, against a 52-week high of US$695.50 per thousand board feet.37 The Signal Dispatch cross-reference engine ties lumber to 269 active forestry projects ($4.7B aggregate) and to British Columbia, Quebec, and Ontario sawmills whose margins track delivered-product pricing.37
